evaluations.questionText: If all Bloops are Razzies and all Razzies are Lazzies, are all Bloops definitely Lazzies? Explain your logical deduction step-by-step.
evaluations.idealAnswer: Yes, all Bloops are definitely Lazzies. By transitive relation in categorical logic: Set A (Bloops) is a subset of Set B (Razzies), and Set B (Razzies) is a subset of Set C (Lazzies). Therefore, any element in Set A must also be contained within Set C (A ⊆ B ⊆ C implies A ⊆ C).

evaluations.questionText: What are the primary differences between Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and Lifetime Value (LTV)? Why is the LTV:CAC ratio crucial?
evaluations.idealAnswer: CAC measures the total sales and marketing spend required to acquire a single paying customer. LTV estimates the total net revenue a customer generates throughout their entire relationship. An LTV:CAC ratio of 3:1 is standard for healthy SaaS businesses. Below 1:1 means the company loses money on every acquisition; excessively high ratios (e.g. 7:1) indicate underinvestment in growth.

evaluations.questionText: A train running at 72 km/h passes a pole in 9 seconds. What is the length of the train in meters? Show your step-by-step calculation.
evaluations.idealAnswer: Step 1: Convert speed from km/h to m/s: 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s. Step 2: Use Distance = Speed * Time. To pass a stationary pole, the train must cover its entire length. Distance = 20 m/s * 9 seconds = 180 meters. Therefore, the length of the train is 180 meters.

evaluations.questionText: What is the probability of drawing either an Ace or a King from a standard deck of 52 playing cards in a single draw?
evaluations.idealAnswer: A standard deck has 52 cards. There are 4 Aces and 4 Kings. Since drawing an Ace and drawing a King are mutually exclusive events, total favorable outcomes = 4 + 4 = 8. Probability = Favorable Outcomes / Total Sample Space = 8 / 52. Simplifying by dividing numerator and denominator by 4 yields 2/13 (approx 15.38%).

currentQuestion.question: Explain the Virtual DOM in React and how reconciliation works when state updates occur.
hints: Mention shadow copy of DOM, diffing algorithm, and batch updates.
currentQuestion.idealAnswer: The Virtual DOM (VDOM) is an in-memory, lightweight JavaScript representation of the actual DOM. When component state changes, React creates a new VDOM tree and compares it to the previous tree using an O(n) heuristic diffing algorithm (Reconciliation). React computes the minimal set of changes (diffs) and batches updates to the real DOM, avoiding expensive layout reflows and browser repaints.
